text: In the Scholium to the Principia, what is the defining feature of Newton's absolute time?
choices: It flows uniformly on its own, independently of matter, motion, and observers, serving as a fixed backdrop for mechanics.
It is an abstraction from the pattern of change among physical objects and has no reality in an empty universe.
It is a dynamical field that is warped and slowed by the presence of matter and energy.
It is defined by the orbital motions of the celestial bodies, as in ephemeris time.
explanation: Newton's absolute time 'flows equably without relation to anything external': it is non-dynamical, independent of matter and observers, and provides the universal background against which motion unfolds. Option 1 is the relational view of Leibniz and Mach, which Newton rejected; option 2 is the dynamical time of general relativity, a much later development; option 3 describes ephemeris or 'common' (relative) time, which Newton regarded as only an approximate measure of the true absolute duration beneath it.
